chapter: Mingus and the call from Hampton
title: Wes substitutes in Hampton's band; how Monk's call came about
summary: Wes filled in for guitarist William Mackel with Lionel Hampton around 1949-50; Monk believes this led to his own call.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, at that point, then, did the three of you become pretty much of a unit?
Yeah, after Buddy came from the army, how was this...
What year is this, that Buddy came back?

Let me put it this way...Let me get the years and things straight, because I'm getting a little confused on the time. Because all three of us were...After I was playing a couple of years -- this is the way it is -- after I was playing a couple years, I got a call to go with Lionel Hampton's band. That scared me to death. Nothing like going to play with Cy Jones, right? Supposed to join Lionel Hampton on the road. So I'm looking at it from a much huger...
Was this after Wes had done the same thing?

Yeah, this was after this. Because Wes worked with Hamp...Wes's was a short period because he took the guitar player's place. See, William Mackel was the guitar player with Hamp, and had been for over the years, up until here recently when he left. And when Mackel got ill at one point, Wes took his place while he was off. Wes worked with him. When he came back, then that was the end of the thing for Hamp for Wes. But that wasn't what Wes wanted to make his career doing. But, boy, he made a hot set there, when he went in.

And I do believe, on the strength of the thing with Wes was how I got the job with Hamp. Because when they came to town, Lionel Hampton came to town about '49 or '50. 1949, 1950, in there. When they came to town, Wes was working with the band and...Boy, that was a...Lionel Hampton, he was big!
